title: Regional hedging & grace-window strategy for limiter outage recovery
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
We need an automated hedging and grace-window mechanism that allows regional limiter outages (partial or full) to fail over traffic while preserving SLOs and preventing long tail amplification. The feature should: allow short, bounded overage admission during resolver convergence; prioritize customer-critical routes; reconcile quotas post-facto; and provide operator controls to adjust grace-window behavior per-region and per-tenant.

Background and motivation:
- Recent incident 2026-01-30: a control-plane replication lag caused EU limiter meta-store to be read-only for ~7 minutes. During that window we observed a) aggressive client retries, b) synchronous global fallback which overloaded US region, and c) a backlog that caused elevated p99s.
- Existing fallback is a blunt "open everything to dedicated tier" which protects availability but caused cost and violated several tenant SLO objectives.
- We need a middle ground between full open failover and hard-deny: a temporally bounded, prioritized hedging window with post-incident quota reconciliation and observability.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  * Ensure availability for high-priority/paid routes during short regional limiter unavailable windows while limiting cascading load to healthy regions.
  * Preserve customer fairness long-term via reconciliation and throttled refund/credit mechanisms.
  * Make behavior configurable by region and tenant tier and exposable in Console.
- Non-goals:
  * This ticket is not about redoing the entire quota model or multi-DC consensus algorithm. It leverages current lease/heartbeat primitives where possible.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Detection: control-plane SRE/serving runtime emits a "limiter-unavailable" event per-region when local limiter health checks fail or meta-store is read-only for more than X seconds (default X=3s).
2) Hedging + Grace Window:
   - On detection, healthy regions enter a coordinated hedging mode for affected tenant namespaces for a configurable grace-window W (default W=120s). During W:
     * Allow a small over-admission budget per-tenant per-second (hedge_rate) that is proportional to their historical ingress rate and tier (paid > standard > free).
     * Admission is strictly bounded: no single tenant can consume more than hedge_burst tokens during the window.
     * New requests from hedged region tag requests with hedged=true in trace context for downstream cost accounting and routing.
   - Requests exceeding hedging limits should be rate-limited with an explicit 429 + Retry-After indicating global degrade state.
3) Prioritization:
   - Maintain a route-level priority map (from Console) that Delta-weights tenants and routes. During hedging, the admission allocator uses the weights for proportional allocation.
4) Reconciliation:
   - After limiter recovers, a reconciliation job runs per-tenant that:
     * computes net over-admitted tokens,
     * decides between delta-credit, token-bill correction, or silent amortization depending on tenant policy,
     * emits reconciliation events and dashboard rows.
5) Operator controls and emergency off-ramps:
   - Console toggles: hedging.enabled, hedge_window_sec, hedge_rate_multiplier_by_tier, hedge_burst_limits, reconciliation_strategy.
   - SRE fast path to disable hedging globally or for a region.

Detailed invariants and constraints:
- Hedging window must not permit unbounded concurrency that violates downstream model-serving SLOs; we will cap hedged admission by an absolute cluster-wide throttle derived from 95th percentile baseline capacity.
- Hedging tokens must be metered separately to enable transparent billing and audit.
- Reconciliation must be eventually consistent and safe to re-run: jobs must be idempotent and produce auditable events.

Metrics and success criteria:
- During a simulated limiter outage test: p95 and p99 request latency in failover region should remain below 2x baseline and < 1s increase for 95% of requests for priority routes.
- No tenant consumes more than hedge_burst limit in any W window in 99.9% of simulations.
- Reconciliation job completes within 5 minutes of limiter recovery for 95% of tenants.
- SLO regression: utility-weighted SLO drop across tenants < 0.5% for these events.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase A (this ticket): detection + hedging admission allocator + telemetry. Implement hedging admission in serving runtime path with simple per-tenant token buckets and a circuit state machine. Add telemetry traces and Console feature flags. Deliver foundational reconciliation scaffolding (event writes).
- Phase B (follow-up): prioritized route maps, advanced reconciliation strategies (credit vs billing), and UI for inspecting hedged events.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for allocator and idempotent reconciliation logic.
- Chaos test scenario: make region B limiter meta-store read-only for 6 minutes; verify hedging and prevent amplification.
- Load-test: run synthetic tenants at varied percentiles and assert hedging invariants.

Rollout and canary:
- Start with hedging.enabled=false. Ship runtime that accepts flags. Enable hedging for internal tenants only in us-west-2 (canary), run for 72 hours.
- Gradual expansion to EU and APAC and to paid customers per manual enable in Console.

Observability and alerts:
- New dashboards: Hedged admissions by region/tenant, hedged vs normal token usage, reconciliation job latency and outcomes, incidents where hedging hit burst limits.
- Alerts: hedging_burst_exhausted_rate > 1% for > 1m, reconciliation_failures > 5 in 10m, hedging_enabled_but_no_traffic on applied tenants.

Open questions and decisions needed:
- What default reconciliation strategy should we prefer for free-tier tenants? (silent amortization vs retroactive accounting)
- Exact sizing formula for hedge_rate and hedge_burst. Proposal: hedge_rate = historical_qps_95 * multiplier_by_tier, hedge_burst = hedge_rate * 10.
- Legal/finance approval required for any post-facto billing delta flows.

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature flagged hedging and basic reconciliation event emission live behind Console toggles.
- Automated unit and integration tests green.
- Canary run in us-west-2 with internal tenants demonstrating no service-level outages and reconciliation job stability.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Hedging+Grace+Window+Design
- PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124
- Console feature flag work: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/989

Notes on backwards compatibility and migration:
- Default behavior remains unchanged until hedging.enabled=true.
- Reconciliation events are append-only and safe for historical billing pipelines that ignore unknown event types.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: hedging allows a tenant to game the system and generate cost by retry storms. Mitigation: tag hedged requests and throttle client-side retries via Retry-After and client SDK education; build a client-side adaptive backoff helper.
- Risk: reconciliation backlog under heavy incidents. Mitigation: limit catch-up rate and prioritize higher value tenants.

Next steps / TODOs:
- (A) Finalize hedge_rate formula with SRE and PM (owner: Luca).
- (B) Complete PR 3124 and add unit tests for idempotency (owner: Aisha).
- (C) Add Console toggles and basic UI for hedging metrics (owner: Maya Patel, PM).
